$V_0 < V_1 < \cdots$ such that each $V_n$ is generated as a verbal subgroup
by one element $w_n$?

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 5.42

by A. Yu. Ol'shanskiĭ

Does the free group of rank $2$ have an infinite strictly ascending chain of
verbal subgroups, each generated as a verbal subgroup by a single element?

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«5.42»

/-- The verbal subgroup of a group $G$ generated by one element $w$: the subgroup
generated by all values of $w$ under endomorphisms of $G$. -/
def verbalSubgroupGeneratedBy {G : Type*} [Group G] (w : G) : Subgroup G :=
  Subgroup.closure (Set.range fun f : G →* G => f w)

/--
Does the free group of rank $2$ have an infinite strictly ascending chain of
verbal subgroups, each generated as a verbal subgroup by a single element?

Here the verbal subgroup generated by $w$ is the smallest fully invariant
normal subgroup containing $w$. The condition at every $n$ makes the chain
strictly increasing.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«5.42» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ w : ℕ → FreeGroup (Fin 2),
      ∀ n : ℕ, verbalSubgroupGeneratedBy (w n) < verbalSubgroupGeneratedBy (w (n + 1)) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«5.42»
modeling_decisions: The free group of rank 2 is represented as `FreeGroup (Fin 2)`.

A verbal subgroup generated by one word `w` is represented by the subgroup closure of all endomorphic images of `w`; for a free group these endomorphisms encode arbitrary substitutions, and closure under inner endomorphisms makes the subgroup normal.
An infinite strictly ascending chain is represented by a sequence of words indexed by `ℕ` whose associated verbal subgroups are strictly included at every successor index.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 5.42

by A. Yu. Ol'shanskiĭ

Does the free group of rank 2 have an infinite ascending chain of verbal subgroups
each being generated as a verbal subgroup by a single element?

Here, for a word $w$ (an element of a free group $F(X)$) and a group $G$, the verbal
subgroup $w(G)$ of $G$ defined by $w$ is the subgroup generated by all values
$\varphi(w)$ of $w$ in $G$, where $\varphi$ ranges over all homomorphisms
$F(X) \to G$. For an element $v$ of the free group $F_2$ of rank 2, the verbal
subgroup of $F_2$ generated by $v$ is $v(F_2)$, the subgroup generated by the
images of $v$ under all endomorphisms of $F_2$; it is the smallest fully invariant
subgroup of $F_2$ containing $v$.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«5.42»

variable {α : Type*} {G : Type*} [Group G]

/-- The verbal subgroup $w(G)$ of a group $G$ defined by a single word $w \in F(\alpha)$:
the subgroup of $G$ generated by all values $\varphi(w)$ of $w$ in $G$, where $\varphi$
ranges over all homomorphisms $F(\alpha) \to G$. -/
def verbalSubgroup (w : FreeGroup α) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Subgroup G :=
  Subgroup.closure (Set.range fun φ : FreeGroup α →* G => φ w)

/-- A word lies in the verbal subgroup of the free group that it defines. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem self_mem_verbalSubgroup (w : FreeGroup α) : w ∈ verbalSubgroup w (FreeGroup α) :=
  Subgroup.subset_closure ⟨MonoidHom.id _, rfl⟩

/-- The verbal subgroup defined by the trivial word is trivial. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem verbalSubgroup_one : verbalSubgroup (1 : FreeGroup α) G = ⊥ :=
  le_bot_iff.1 <| (Subgroup.closure_le ⊥).2 <| by rintro _ ⟨φ, rfl⟩; simp

/-- Verbal subgroups are fully invariant: they are mapped into themselves by every
endomorphism. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem verbalSubgroup_map_le (w : FreeGroup α) (ψ : G →* G) :
    (verbalSubgroup w G).map ψ ≤ verbalSubgroup w G := by
  rw [Subgroup.map_le_iff_le_comap]
  refine (Subgroup.closure_le _).2 ?_
  rintro _ ⟨φ, rfl⟩
  exact Subgroup.subset_closure ⟨ψ.comp φ, rfl⟩

/-- Verbal subgroups are normal. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem verbalSubgroup_normal (w : FreeGroup α) : (verbalSubgroup w G).Normal where
  conj_mem _ hn g :=
    verbalSubgroup_map_le w (MulAut.conj g).toMonoidHom (Subgroup.mem_map_of_mem _ hn)

/--
Does the free group of rank 2 have an infinite ascending chain of verbal subgroups
each being generated as a verbal subgroup by a single element?

That is, do there exist elements $w_0, w_1, w_2, \dots$ of the free group $F_2$ of rank 2
such that the verbal subgroups $w_n(F_2)$ generated by them form a strictly ascending
chain $w_0(F_2) < w_1(F_2) < w_2(F_2) < \cdots$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«5.42» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ w : ℕ → FreeGroup (Fin 2),
      StrictMono fun n => verbalSubgroup (w n) (FreeGroup (Fin 2)) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«5.42»
attempts.decomposition_objections: None. The single-slot decomposition matches the statement; the notes' reading (strict chain, verbal subgroup = endomorphism-closed subgroup generated by the word's values) is the standard one and is what the file formalizes.
modeling_decisions: 'Infinite ascending chain' is read as a strictly increasing ℕ-indexed sequence V_0 < V_1 < V_2 < ⋯ (`StrictMono`). Any infinite chain with infinitely many distinct members contains such a subsequence, so this is not a restriction.

'Generated as a verbal subgroup by a single element' is read as: the single element is an element v of F_2 itself, and the verbal subgroup it generates is ⟨φ(v) : φ ∈ End(F_2)⟩ (all values of v under all substitutions in F_2), exactly as in the decomposition notes. Since this set of images is closed under further endomorphisms, this equals the smallest fully invariant subgroup of F_2 containing v.

The definition `verbalSubgroup` is stated generally for a word w ∈ FreeGroup α and an arbitrary group G (homomorphisms FreeGroup α →* G), then specialised to α = Fin 2 and G = FreeGroup (Fin 2); with these parameters the homomorphisms are exactly the endomorphisms of F_2.
The bespoke definition is kept in the problem file (the task allows writing only one file); a reviewer may prefer moving it to FormalConjecturesForMathlib as it is reusable.
The free group of rank 2 is modelled as `FreeGroup (Fin 2)`.

/-!
# Conjecture 5.42

by A. Yu. Ol'shanskiĭ

Does the free group of rank 2 have an infinite ascending chain of
verbal subgroups each being generated as a verbal subgroup by a
single element?

For an element $w$ of a group $G$, the verbal subgroup of $G$ generated by $w$
is the subgroup generated by all images $\varphi(w)$ of $w$ under endomorphisms
$\varphi$ of $G$. It is the smallest fully invariant subgroup of $G$ containing
$w$. When $G = F_2$ is the free group of rank $2$ and $w \in F_2$ is viewed as
a word in two variables, the values of $w$ in $F_2$ are exactly the images of
$w$ under endomorphisms of $F_2$, so this is the usual verbal subgroup $w(F_2)$.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«5.42»

variable {G : Type*} [Group G]

/-- The verbal subgroup of a group $G$ generated by a single element $w$: the
subgroup generated by all images $\varphi(w)$ of $w$ under endomorphisms
$\varphi$ of $G$. -/
def verbalSubgroup (w : G) : Subgroup G :=
  Subgroup.closure (Set.range fun φ : G →* G => φ w)

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem self_mem_verbalSubgroup (w : G) : w ∈ verbalSubgroup w :=
  Subgroup.subset_closure ⟨MonoidHom.id G, rfl⟩

/-- The verbal subgroup generated by $w$ is fully invariant: it is mapped into
itself by every endomorphism of $G$. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem map_verbalSubgroup_le (φ : G →* G) (w : G) :
    (verbalSubgroup w).map φ ≤ verbalSubgroup w := by
  rw [verbalSubgroup, MonoidHom.map_closure]
  refine (Subgroup.closure_le _).mpr ?_
  rintro _ ⟨_, ⟨ψ, rfl⟩, rfl⟩
  exact Subgroup.subset_closure ⟨φ.comp ψ, rfl⟩

/-- The verbal subgroup generated by $w$ is the smallest fully invariant
subgroup of $G$ containing $w$. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem verbalSubgroup_le_iff (w : G) (H : Subgroup G) (hH : ∀ φ : G →* G, H.map φ ≤ H) :
    verbalSubgroup w ≤ H ↔ w ∈ H := by
  refine ⟨fun h => h (self_mem_verbalSubgroup w), fun hw => (Subgroup.closure_le _).mpr ?_⟩
  rintro _ ⟨φ, rfl⟩
  exact hH φ ⟨w, hw, rfl⟩

/--
Does the free group of rank 2 have an infinite ascending chain of verbal
subgroups each being generated as a verbal subgroup by a single element?

That is, are there elements $w_0, w_1, w_2, \ldots$ of the free group $F_2$ of
rank $2$ whose verbal subgroups form a strictly increasing chain
$w_0(F_2) < w_1(F_2) < w_2(F_2) < \cdots$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«5.42» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ w : ℕ → FreeGroup (Fin 2), StrictMono fun n => verbalSubgroup (w n) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«5.42»
modeling_decisions: 'Generated as a verbal subgroup by a single element' is read, following the decomposition notes, as: the generating element is an element w of F_2 itself and the subgroup is the smallest fully invariant subgroup of F_2 containing w. For a free group this coincides with the verbal subgroup w(F_2) of the 2-variable word w, since the values of w in F_2 are exactly its images under endomorphisms of F_2. An alternative reading, in which the single generating word lives in a free group of higher/infinite rank (i.e. V(F_2) for a variety V defined by a single law), was not adopted; a reviewer should confirm the chosen reading.
'Infinite ascending chain' is formalized as an ℕ-indexed strictly increasing sequence (StrictMono), per the decomposition note that 'ascending' should be strict.
The free group of rank 2 is taken as FreeGroup (Fin 2) (the standard choice; the statement is invariant under the choice of 2-element index type).
Extra proved API lemmas for the bespoke definition are included in the problem file, following CONTRIBUTING.md's request for basic API tests; they contain no sorry.

/-!
# Conjecture 5.42

by A. Yu. Ol'shanskiĭ

Does the free group of rank 2 have an infinite ascending chain of verbal subgroups each being
generated as a verbal subgroup by a single element?

Here the verbal subgroup of a group $G$ determined by a set $W$ of words is the subgroup
generated by all values of the words in $W$ on $G$. For a single word $w \in F_2$ the verbal
subgroup of $F_2$ it determines is the subgroup generated by all images $\varphi(w)$ of $w$
under endomorphisms $\varphi$ of $F_2$; this is the smallest fully invariant (equivalently,
verbal) subgroup of $F_2$ containing $w$.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«5.42»

/-- The verbal subgroup $W(G)$ of a group $G$ determined by a set $W$ of words in the free group
on `ι`: the subgroup of $G$ generated by all values $\varphi(w)$ of words $w \in W$ under all
homomorphisms $\varphi$ from the free group to $G$, that is, under all substitutions of elements
of $G$ for the variables. -/
def verbalSubgroup {ι : Type*} (W : Set (FreeGroup ι)) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Subgroup G :=
  Subgroup.closure {g | ∃ w ∈ W, ∃ φ : FreeGroup ι →* G, φ w = g}

variable {ι : Type*} (W : Set (FreeGroup ι)) {G : Type*} [Group G]

/-- A value of a word in `W` lies in the verbal subgroup determined by `W`. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem apply_mem_verbalSubgroup {w : FreeGroup ι} (hw : w ∈ W) (φ : FreeGroup ι →* G) :
    φ w ∈ verbalSubgroup W G :=
  Subgroup.subset_closure ⟨w, hw, φ, rfl⟩

/-- Verbal subgroups are fully invariant: they are mapped into themselves by every
endomorphism. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem verbalSubgroup_map_le (f : G →* G) :
    (verbalSubgroup W G).map f ≤ verbalSubgroup W G := by
  rw [verbalSubgroup, MonoidHom.map_closure]
  refine Subgroup.closure_mono fun g hg => ?_
  obtain ⟨_, ⟨w, hw, φ, rfl⟩, rfl⟩ := hg
  exact ⟨w, hw, f.comp φ, rfl⟩

/-- Verbal subgroups are normal. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
instance verbalSubgroup_normal : (verbalSubgroup W G).Normal where
  conj_mem n hn g := verbalSubgroup_map_le W (MulAut.conj g).toMonoidHom ⟨n, hn, rfl⟩

/-- For a single word `w` in the free group of rank 2, the verbal subgroup of the free group of
rank 2 it determines is generated by the images of `w` under all endomorphisms. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem verbalSubgroup_singleton_freeGroup (w : FreeGroup (Fin 2)) :

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 5.42

by A. Yu. Ol'shanskiĭ

Does the free group of rank 2 have an infinite ascending chain of verbal subgroups
each being generated as a verbal subgroup by a single element?

For an element $w$ of a group $G$, the verbal subgroup of $G$ generated by $w$ is the
subgroup generated by all values $\varphi(w)$ of $w$ under the endomorphisms
$\varphi$ of $G$. It is the smallest fully invariant (i.e. endomorphism-closed) subgroup
of $G$ containing $w$; in particular it is normal.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«5.42»

variable {G : Type*} [Group G]

/-- The verbal subgroup of $G$ generated by the single element $w$: the subgroup generated by
all values $\varphi(w)$ of $w$ under endomorphisms $\varphi$ of $G$. -/
def verbalSubgroup (w : G) : Subgroup G :=
  Subgroup.closure (Set.range fun φ : G →* G => φ w)

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem self_mem_verbalSubgroup (w : G) : w ∈ verbalSubgroup w :=
  Subgroup.subset_closure ⟨MonoidHom.id G, rfl⟩

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem verbalSubgroup_one : verbalSubgroup (1 : G) = ⊥ := by
  simp [verbalSubgroup]

/-- The verbal subgroup generated by `w` is fully invariant. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem map_verbalSubgroup_le (w : G) (ψ : G →* G) :
    (verbalSubgroup w).map ψ ≤ verbalSubgroup w := by
  rw [Subgroup.map_le_iff_le_comap, verbalSubgroup, Subgroup.closure_le]
  rintro _ ⟨φ, rfl⟩
  exact Subgroup.subset_closure ⟨ψ.comp φ, rfl⟩

/-- The verbal subgroup generated by `w` is the smallest fully invariant subgroup
containing `w`. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem verbalSubgroup_le_iff {w : G} {H : Subgroup G} (hH : ∀ ψ : G →* G, H.map ψ ≤ H) :
    verbalSubgroup w ≤ H ↔ w ∈ H := by
  refine ⟨fun h => h (self_mem_verbalSubgroup w), fun hw => ?_⟩
  rw [verbalSubgroup, Subgroup.closure_le]
  rintro _ ⟨φ, rfl⟩
  exact hH φ ⟨w, hw, rfl⟩

@[category API, AMS 20]
instance verbalSubgroup_normal (w : G) : (verbalSubgroup w).Normal where
  conj_mem n hn g := map_verbalSubgroup_le w (MulAut.conj g).toMonoidHom ⟨n, hn, rfl⟩

/-- The verbal subgroup of the free group of rank 2 generated by a free generator is the whole
group. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem verbalSubgroup_of : verbalSubgroup (FreeGroup.of (0 : Fin 2)) = ⊤ :=
  eq_top_iff.2 fun g _ => Subgroup.subset_closure ⟨FreeGroup.lift fun _ => g, by simp⟩

/--
Does the free group of rank 2 have an infinite ascending chain of verbal subgroups
each being generated as a verbal subgroup by a single element?

That is, are there elements $w_0, w_1, w_2, \ldots$ of the free group $F_2$ of rank 2 whose
verbal subgroups form a strictly ascending chain $V(w_0) < V(w_1) < V(w_2) < \cdots$, where
$V(w)$ is the subgroup of $F_2$ generated by all values $\varphi(w)$ of $w$ under the
endomorphisms $\varphi$ of $F_2$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«5.42» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ w : ℕ → FreeGroup (Fin 2), StrictMono fun n => verbalSubgroup (w n) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«5.42»

modeling_decisions: 'Single element' is read as an element of the free group F₂ itself (a word in the two free generators), with the verbal subgroup it generates being ⟨φ(w) : φ ∈ End(F₂)⟩, as prescribed by the decomposition notes. An alternative reading would allow w to be a word in arbitrarily many variables (an element of F_∞) with values taken under all homomorphisms F_∞ → F₂; the two readings are not obviously equivalent, so a reviewer should confirm the chosen one.
'Ascending' is read as strictly ascending (StrictMono on an ℕ-indexed sequence), following the decomposition notes; a non-strict reading would make the question trivial.
The chain is indexed by ℕ (order type ω), the standard meaning of an infinite ascending chain.

Verbal subgroups of F₂ coincide with fully invariant subgroups of F₂ (every verbal subgroup is fully invariant, and a fully invariant H equals the verbal subgroup defined by the word set H), so 'the verbal subgroup generated by w' is unambiguous: it is the smallest fully invariant subgroup containing w, which the API lemma verbalSubgroup_le_iff certifies for the chosen definition.
The definition is stated for an arbitrary group G (with variable {G : Type*} [Group G]) and kept in the problem file inside the problem namespace, since it is used only by this problem.

/-!
# Conjecture 5.42

by A. Yu. Ol'shanskiĭ

Does the free group of rank $2$ have an infinite strictly ascending chain of
verbal subgroups, each generated as a verbal subgroup by a single element?

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«5.42»

/-- The verbal subgroup generated by one element $w$: the smallest normal
subgroup containing $w$ that is preserved by every endomorphism of the ambient
group. For a free group, endomorphisms are precisely substitutions for the free
generators, so this is the subgroup generated by all substitution values of
$w$. -/
def verbalSubgroupGeneratedBy {G : Type*} [Group G] (w : G) : Subgroup G :=
  sInf {H : Subgroup G | H.Normal ∧ w ∈ H ∧ ∀ f : G →* G, H.map f ≤ H}

/--
Does the free group of rank $2$ have an infinite strictly ascending chain of
verbal subgroups, each generated as a verbal subgroup by a single element?

The rank-$2$ free group is represented by `FreeGroup (Fin 2)`. For each $n$,
the element $w_n$ generates the corresponding verbal subgroup through all
endomorphic images, and `StrictMono` says that these subgroups form a strictly
ascending chain.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«5.42» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ w : ℕ → FreeGroup (Fin 2),
      StrictMono (fun n ↦ verbalSubgroupGeneratedBy (w n)) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«5.42»
modeling_decisions: The free group of rank 2 is modeled as `FreeGroup (Fin 2)`.

A verbal subgroup generated by one element is modeled as the infimum of all normal subgroups containing that element and preserved by every endomorphism of the ambient group. For a free group, these endomorphisms represent all substitutions of the free generators.
The infinite ascending chain is represented by a natural-number-indexed sequence of generating words whose associated verbal subgroups form a `StrictMono` sequence; thus every inclusion is strict.
The yes/no question is represented with `answer(sorry) ↔` followed by the positive existence statement.
